claims.explanation: RITA binds p53 and disrupts its interaction with MDM2, leading to p53 accumulation and activation of pro-apoptotic programs. Selectivity is therefore expected for tumor cells that retain wild-type p53 and have intact apoptotic signaling; TP53 mutations or defects in p53 pathway components (e.g., MDM2 amplification, loss of CDKN1A/p21, or high NF-κB/STAT3 activity) would confer resistance. The virtual cell response showing upregulation of PMAIP1 (NOXA) and downregulation of NRIP1/NCOA3 further supports a p53-dependent apoptotic mechanism.

features.basis: RITA requires wild-type p53 to induce apoptosis; TP53 mutations abolish response.
MDM2 overexpression can sequester p53 and limit RITA's ability to disrupt the complex.
p21 induction promotes cell-cycle arrest over apoptosis; MDM2-mediated p21 degradation is required for RITA-induced apoptosis.
NOXA is a p53 target and pro-apoptotic; its upregulation in virtual cell response indicates apoptotic priming.
STAT3 antagonizes p53-mediated repression of genes including AURKA, potentially blunting RITA response.
AURKA is repressed by p53; high AURKA may promote survival and counteract p53 effects.
p53-induced ULBP1 enhances NK cell-mediated killing; may contribute to RITA efficacy in vivo.
p53-induced ULBP2 enhances NK cell-mediated killing; may contribute to RITA efficacy in vivo.
p63 isoforms can act similarly to p53 and may compensate or enhance response to RITA.
p73 isoforms can act similarly to p53 and may compensate or enhance response to RITA.
